name: weight_averaging_sel1m_v1
purpose: Does averaging model weights reduce the epoch-to-epoch noise of the selected checkpoint and improve it? For each step 2 run, a fixed list of weight averages is scored on sel1m_tail with the same evaluation as the plain selected checkpoint; the best of them (or the plain checkpoint) is the run's averaged selection. The holdout set is used only afterwards, once per run, in holdout_sel1m_avg_v1. Every arm gets the same recipes.
rules: e is the selected epoch and M the selected member (manifest best, the rule of holdout_sel1m_v1).

lineage_window: uniform average of the checkpoints of M's ancestry at epochs e-before .. e+after. Before a copy into M, the ancestry continues in the donor; after e it is M's own later checkpoints. The window is cut at the first trained epoch and the last epoch.

greedy_population_soup: the members' epoch-e checkpoints, without members that received a copy at epoch e, ordered by their training-time sel1m metric; start from the best one, add each next one if the uniform average scores better on sel1m_tail.

All candidates, the plain checkpoint included, are scored by the same Weaver test-mode evaluation on sel1m_tail. The candidate with the lowest primary metric is the run's averaged selection; ties go to the earlier recipe in the list.
Runs whose selection is plain are not evaluated again on the holdout set; their holdout_sel1m_v1 result stands.
